intro: Athletic trainers assess injuries, teach recovery and make quick decisions on the sideline, skills shared with therapy careers. The closest of the 25 careers below are Physical Therapists and Exercise Physiologists, both at a 90% match; physical therapists earn a BLS May 2025 median of $102,760, or 64% more than the $62,520 athletic trainers earn.
why_it_works: Working with athletes means preventing injuries, treating them fast and guiding people back to full strength. O*NET rates judgment at 3.88 out of 5 for this job, social perceptiveness at 3.75 and instructing at 3.62. Physical and occupational therapy use the same knowledge of the body. All 25 matches need no more education than you have, though licenses differ. The gaps are coordination and operations.
tips: Physical therapy is the closest well-paid move; check which of your courses count toward a DPT program.
Occupational Therapists earn $100,330, which is 60% more, and are an 87% match.
Teaching in a health program pays $107,310, or 72% more, and suits experienced trainers.

faq.q: What jobs can former athletic trainers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Physical Therapists (90%), Exercise Physiologists (90%) and Occupational Therapists (87%), based on O*NET 31.0. Physical Therapist Assistants are 84% matched and earn $68,380, which is 9% more than the $62,520 athletic trainer median.

faq.q: Which careers for athletic trainers pay more?
faq.a: 15 of the 25 matches pay more. Nurse Anesthetists earn $236,590 (278% more), health specialties teachers $107,310 (72% more) and Physical Therapists $102,760 (64% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Nurse anesthesia requires nursing school and graduate training first, so it is a long path.

faq.q: Do athletic trainers need another degree to switch?
faq.a: Not more education in general: all 25 matches need no more than athletic trainers already have. A doctoral degree is common in the closest match, held by 47% of workers, and each therapy career needs its own license, so plan for an exam even when the degree level matches.

faq.q: What skills should athletic trainers learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are coordination, operations analysis, repairing and service orientation. Instructing already rates 3.62 out of 5 for athletic trainers in O*NET, so clinical depth and program management are the main steps for most moves.
